topics.title: Stern’s Cleveland Broadcast – Book Title Dispute
topics.summary: During last week's broadcast, Howard Stern expanded his radio show to Cleveland while discussing a complicated relationship with Mia Farrow and initially naming a book ‘Black Like Me.’ Despite disagreements over the title—which he ultimately settled on after publisher concerns—Stern fielded questions from reporters about potential offensive content and made several humorous remarks regarding Oliver Stone.

topics.title: Tape Testimonial Reveals Nazi Cartoon & Terrorist Threat
topics.summary: During a phone-in segment, Howard plays a tape featuring Tom Metzger reading from his controversial ‘White Area Race’ cartoon detailing anti-Black sentiments and violent rhetoric. Red joins the conversation offering inflammatory opinions about terrorism and foreign influence, further escalating the discussion with comments regarding the World Trade Center bombing.

topics.title: Terrorist Accusations & Jury Concerns
topics.summary: Howard Stone expresses concerns about terrorism, alleging connections between individuals and questioning the legitimacy of certain religions. He criticizes FBI inaction, demands specific jury demographics to ensure fair trials, and makes outlandish claims regarding punishment for convicted offenders while expressing skepticism towards eyewitness testimony.

topics.title: Step Aerobics and Cher’s TV Dreams
topics.summary: Howard discusses D. Snyder’s ‘share step’ aerobic program recommended by a former Twisted Sister collaborator, detailing the awkwardness of mimicking movements on a wooden platform while attempting to sweat. He then shifts to Cher's plans for her own talk show and promoting hair products, highlighting her outspoken nature and potential controversy.

topics.title: Cher’s Step Aerobic Video & Advertiser Interference
topics.summary: Howard discusses a listener's obsession with Cher’s exercise video and suggestions for protective gear like pulse meters before addressing advertising interference from competitors complaining about the show; he then promotes Fortunoff’s 1993 Summer Swatch Collection, highlighting specific watch styles and encouraging viewers to purchase them.

topics.title: Fred & Jackie Promote Comedy Shows, Cher Critique
topics.summary: During a radio show, Fred the Elephant Boy and Jackie Platinum promote upcoming comedy shows at Wadsworth Theatre in Los Angeles and Levittown, Long Island, while also discussing personal grievances involving Cher’s appearance – particularly her oversized teeth and lips. They briefly discuss discontinued VHS tapes of ‘Butt Bongo Fiesta’ before moving on to a lengthy discussion about the public's reaction to Cher’s facial features.

topics.title: Trump Hotels Four-Star Ratings Debate
topics.summary: During the Howard Stern Show, callers discuss Donald Trump’s hotels receiving four-star ratings despite their locations and amenities. The conversation centers on a comparison between Trump's Atlantic City properties – including the Taj Mahal, Plaza, and Castle – which earned this rating alongside the Mirage Hotel in Las Vegas (three stars), highlighting the perceived difference in quality.

topics.title: Snapple, Jackie West & Nail Infections
topics.summary: During a chaotic radio segment, Howard discusses his wife’s purchase of Snapple iced tea and lemonade, followed by an outlandish story about Jackie West’s bedroom filled with pictures requiring communication via a portable phone. The conversation unexpectedly shifts to concerns regarding potential HIV transmission through fingernail infections, fueled by speculation from callers.

topics.title: FBI Arrests Suspect Linked to World Trade Center Bombing
topics.summary: FBI agents arrested a suspect connected to the World Trade Center bombing after finding rental records and nitrates, suggesting involvement in explosive materials. The arrest followed leaks to newspapers prompting an early action; officials debated immigration policies while investigating potential threats from individuals on tourist visas.

topics.title: Waco Standoff & Iranian Threats - TDK Challenge
topics.summary: During the broadcast, a discussion arose regarding federal statutes and potential death penalties for illegal immigrants in light of Waco events. Red attempted to identify audio clips using TDK tapes with varying results, while concerns were raised about perceived threats from Iran and ongoing tensions surrounding David Koresh's standoff.

topics.title: Step Aerobics, Butt Troubles & Legal Quandaries
topics.summary: The hosts discuss the whereabouts of one of them and attempts to get step aerobics video from Gary, leading into a debate about Jean Harris’s case. They then delve into the Glenridge rape trial involving four teenagers and a woman with limited cognitive abilities, exploring questions of consent and legal definitions.

topics.title: Marshall Tucker Tribute & Offensive Remarks
topics.summary: The broadcast begins with a tribute to Marshall Tucker band founder Toy, followed by an inappropriate segment discussing cowboy hats and making racially charged statements. The show also includes a brief obituary for the musician alongside commentary on country music trends and fan reactions, punctuated by offensive language.

topics.title: Racist Hat Discussions and Offensive Remarks
topics.summary: A radio segment features a chaotic discussion centered around ‘nigger hatin’ hats, with callers expressing racist views about Black people and their attire. The conversation includes violent imagery, dismissive stereotypes, and references to Malcolm X, culminating in an advertisement for Billy West's comedy show.
